title: TaxonomyEntry
description: A community-submittable semantic taxonomy entry: 'raw events matching this topic pattern, emitted by contracts in this scope, mean this'. Maps a contract's raw Soroban event topics onto a human-readable, dot-namespaced taxonomy name (swap.executed, payment.sent, loan.liquidated) with an explicit parameter projection and traceable provenance. This schema is the normative artifact a submission is validated against in review; @orbital-stellar/abi-registry's validateTaxonomyEntry() is the equivalent runtime check for consumers who do not want a JSON Schema validator.

id.description: Stable lowercase kebab-case slug, unique across the published set. Referenced by other entries' `supersedes` and by review tooling, so it must not change once published - rename by superseding, not by editing.

version.description: Semantic version of this entry. Bump it whenever `match` or `parameters` change, since consumers key decoding behaviour off them.

title.description: Short human-readable label for UIs, e.g. "Swap executed".

description.description: What the event means, in prose, for reviewers and consumers.

parameters.description: The taxonomy parameters this entry projects out of the raw event, keyed by lowercase snake_case parameter name. Two entries sharing a taxonomy name should project the same parameter names - that consistency is the whole point of a shared taxonomy.

supersedes.description: IDs of entries this one replaces. Declaring a supersession is what makes an otherwise-conflicting overlap legal: without it, two entries whose patterns and scopes coincide are a collision (see the collision policy on TaxonomyName).

deprecated.description: Set once an entry is retired but kept published so historical events can still be decoded.

TaxonomyName.description: Dot-namespaced taxonomy name. NAMING RULES. Shape: two or three dot-separated segments, `<root>.<action>` or `<root>.<subject>.<action>` - one segment carries no information, four is a sign the concept belongs under a different root. Casing: lowercase ASCII snake_case within a segment, starting with a letter; no uppercase, no hyphens, no leading digits. Namespace root: the first segment must come from the closed list in this pattern - account, asset, bridge, claimable, contract, data, governance, loan, lp, nft, offer, oracle, payment, stake, swap, trustline, vault. The list is closed deliberately: an open-ended root would let two submissions describe one concept under different names (swap.executed vs dex.swapped), which is exactly what a shared taxonomy exists to prevent, so adding a root is a reviewed schema change rather than a per-submission decision. Several roots (account, asset, claimable, contract, data, lp, offer, payment, trustline) already carry meaning in @orbital-stellar/pulse-core's NormalizedEvent taxonomy - a contract-event mapping that means the same thing must reuse the established name rather than mint a parallel one. RESERVED: `engine` and `event` are permanently unavailable, as they are pulse-core's own library diagnostics (engine.reconnecting, event.decode_failed) which describe the indexer rather than the chain. Action segment: use a past-tense verb (executed, liquidated, deposited) - a taxonomy name names something that happened. Tense is a review convention, not machine-checkable. COLLISION POLICY: a taxonomy name is not unique across entries - payment.sent legitimately has one entry per token implementation. Uniqueness is a property of (match pattern, scope): two entries whose patterns match identically within scopes that can cover the same contract are a collision, reported as `ambiguous-mapping` when the names differ and `duplicate-mapping` when they agree, unless one lists the other in `supersedes`. Scopes of different kinds are not compared automatically - deciding whether a specific contract ID is also covered by a wasmHash or SEP-interface scope requires on-chain state, so that overlap is a reviewer's judgment call. `findTaxonomyConflicts()` in @orbital-stellar/abi-registry implements the machine-checkable half.

PrimitiveType.description: An atomic Soroban scalar type. Same set as ContractSpec's PrimitiveType in spec.schema.json.

Network.description: Network a scope is restricted to.

TopicMatcher.description: One positional slot in a raw event's topic vector. Matchers decide whether an entry applies to an event; they never extract values. Extraction is ParameterMapping's job, keyed by topic index - keeping the two separate means a pattern can be tightened without silently re-binding a parameter.

oneOf.description: The topic must be exactly this symbol. Conventionally slot 0, which carries the event name.
Any single topic, optionally constrained to one Soroban scalar type.

TaxonomyMatch.description: The raw-event pattern this entry applies to.

trailingTopics.description: Whether topics beyond the listed matchers are tolerated. Defaults to "forbidden" - a stricter pattern is the safer default for a mapping consumers will trust. "allowed" is the right choice for SEP-41 events on Stellar Asset Contracts, where CAP-67 appends an `asset` topic that a contract-token event does not have.

dataShape.description: Optional constraint on the data payload's shape. "scalar" covers a single value (SEP-41's i128 amount), "map" covers CAP-67-style keyed data. Omit to leave unconstrained.

ParameterMapping.description: Where one taxonomy parameter's value comes from in the raw event.

oneOf.description: A topic slot, by index into the raw topic vector.

index.description: Zero-based index into the raw topic vector.

oneOf.description: The data payload. Use `path` to select a key for map-shaped data (dotted for nesting); omit it to take the whole data value, as SEP-41's bare i128 amount requires.

A fixed value the raw event does not carry. This is how one raw event maps onto a taxonomy name more specific than the event itself - e.g. direction: "out" distinguishing the sender's view of a transfer.

TaxonomyScope.description: Which deployed contracts this entry applies to. `contract` is narrowest and always safe. `wasmHash` covers every deployment of one reviewed build, the honest scope for a protocol that deploys the same code many times. `interface` is broadest - it applies to anything implementing the named SEP - and must only be used for events the SEP itself defines, never for a protocol's own extensions.

contractIds.description: Specific deployed contract addresses this entry applies to.

wasmHashes.description: Hex-encoded SHA-256 hashes of the reviewed WASM builds this entry applies to.

interface.description: SEP interface identifier, e.g. "SEP-41". Only events the SEP itself defines may be scoped this way.

TaxonomyProvenance.description: Who submitted this entry, when, and on what basis. The taxonomy is published as open data, so a claim with no traceable source is not reviewable.

submittedBy.description: GitHub handle (@octocat) or Stellar account address (G…) of the submitter.

sources.description: At least one URL backing the claim: protocol docs, the contract's source, an audit, or an explorer link to a real emitted event.

reviewedBy.description: Handles of the maintainers who accepted the entry.
